Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  March 6, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council Chambers
located on the ninth floor of City Hall on March 6, 2025. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting
to order at 6:03 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Ashley Ferrette announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio
  Padilla - District 2, Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4
  Absent:  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3, Commissioner
  Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada  Assistant Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Marisela Mansour  Human Services Operations Manager
  Juan Mata  Park Maintenance Supervisor
  Ashley Ferrette  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Denmon and second by Commissioner Padilla
that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on February 6, 2025,
be approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:

Ayes: Commissioners Padilla, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Park Maintenance Supervisor Juan Mata reported the
following: Park Maintenance – we recently installed two bike racks, one at Darby Park and the
other at Edward Vincent Park. We have a third concrete slab that will be installed at Edward
Vincent Park. Tree Maintenance – Our city tree crews are working through each district, focusing
on trees that are not scheduled for full trimming until 2027. Any tree requiring immediate attention
will receive a safety trim to ensure proper clearance for pedestrians and vehicles. Meanwhile, our
tree trimming contractor, West Cost Arborists, is completing work along Pincay and Crenshaw and
will begin the annual trimming of ficus trees next week. Graffiti Abatement – to report all graffiti
incidences, the Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

REPORT - RECREATION. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Assistant Director Teresa
Estrada reported the following: Sports Update - the Inglewood Youth Sports League continues to
positively impact the youth in our community. Our Sports Supervisor, Anthony Harris continues to
do an outstanding job in providing sports opportunities for our youth. He and his dedicated team
work year-round to ensure that our residents have access to exceptional sports and programs that
foster teamwork, skill development, and a love for the game. Their commitment to creating
meaningful recreational experiences truly enhances the quality of life for the youth in our
community. We are currently in the midst of our Youth Basketball Season, which offers
opportunities for both boys and girls ages 4 to 14. This season, we have an impressive 391
participants. The season will run through April 11. While our Youth Basketball season is currently
underway, we are also running our Youth Soccer program, which provides opportunities for boys
and girls ages 4 to 12. This season, we have 214 enthusiastic players participating. Practices take
place during the week, with the games being held on weekends. The season will continue through
the coming weeks and is set to conclude on April 19. The Sports Division is currently promoting our
Dodgers Dream team Tee Ball and Coach Pitch "Spring Season." Online registration will be from
March 15th through April 1st. In preparation for the upcoming season, the Inglewood Youth Sports
League will be hosting a "Hitting Clinic" for boys and girls between the ages of 5 and 8. The clinics
will be held on April 3rd and 5th. All interested families can obtain league and clinic details on the
Inglewood Youth Sports League website at: cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com Darby Park Activities
- The department is thrilled to announce a new collaboration and partnership with the Los Angeles
Public Health Department. Through this partnership, we will offer educational and health
workshops tailored to benefit our community. Our primary focus is on our senior population,
particularly those who regularly use the walking path at Darby Park. While we have previously
attempted to host these sessions indoors, we’ve recognized that the majority of participants prefer
to be outdoors. To better meet their needs, we are launching two outdoor classes, the first of
which is Walk with the Nurse. We invite you to join us for a guided health walk and talk, where
participants can stroll around the track while engaging in meaningful discussions with nurses about
important public health topics. This program takes place every second Wednesday of the month
from 9 a.m. to 10 a.m. In addition to our new Walk with the Nurse program, we are also excited to
introduce our Wellness Wednesday classes. These sessions feature specific health and wellness
topics and take place every third Wednesday of the month from 9 to 10 a.m. We invite you to join
us on March 19th for Nutrition for Older Adults, a class designed to provide valuable resources and
information tailored to senior citizens. Additionally, on April 16th, we will host a Falls Prevention
workshop which will offer practical strategies to help reduce the risk of falls and promote safety.
We encourage you or anyone you know who could benefit from these workshops to take
advantage of these valuable opportunities and attend. I am excited about the positive impact that
these classes and resources will have on the well-being of our community. By providing accessible
health education and support, we hope to empower our residents and seniors to lead healthier
lives. I also want to encourage you to attend our upcoming Family Cooking Class on Saturday,
March 22nd, at Rogers Park from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. We are excited to continue our collaboration
with the Youthful Joy Foundation to provide educational health workshops that benefit the entire
family. This workshop is designed to bring families together to learn how to prepare nutritious
meals while fostering healthy eating habits at home. It’s a great opportunity to gain practical
cooking skills, explore healthy food choices, and create lasting wellness habits as a family. I hope
you will join us and spread the word to others who may be interested. Special Events - Lastly, you

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

have all been provided with the 2025 Special Events Schedule. I hope this document serves as a
helpful resource, giving you a clear overview of all events organized by the Parks, Recreation, and
Community Services Department. We are excited about the programs and opportunities ahead
and look forward to your continued support and participation. For more information on our
Inglewood  Youth  Sports  Leagues,  visit  our  city  sports  website  at:
https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Operations Manager Marisela Mansour
reported on the following: Senior Center Operations - Our Senior Center is packed with more
seniors than ever as we continue to grow our participation numbers, as well as increase our
offerings. For March, we have presentations by Grace Farwell of the organization Helping Elderly
Live Productively, or H.E.L.P. for short. On March 7, Grace will be presenting on stress reduction.
On March 21, the topic will be Caregiving Stages and Options, and on March 4 and 25, we will have
a Q & A session with H.E.L.P. We have the Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health
presenting a session on preserving your memory on March 10. OPICACARES will be presenting signs
of dementia on March 26. On March 10, AARP will be providing free tax preparation services for
our seniors. On March 17, we encourage staff and seniors to wear green for St. Patrick’s Day. Our
big annual event, the Black and White Gala, will be on March 21, from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. Attendees
will enjoy an evening of dancing, delicious finger foods, and desserts. Tickets are available on a
first-come, first-served basis at the Senior Center reception desk. Senior Nutrition - We serve
approximately 450 seniors weekly through home delivered meals for homebound seniors and
congregate meals at our Senior Center. We continue to provide fresh produce weekly in
collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute, and monthly shelf stable meal boxes in
collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank. Child and Adult Care Food Program - The Child and
Adult Care Food Program, informally CACFP, serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and
operates at Crenshaw Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park. The program's hours are Monday
through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM and snacks from 4:30 PM - 5:00 PM. We
serve an average of 115 suppers and 50 snacks per week. Senior Transportation - The City of
Inglewood’s paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled community
in Inglewood and Hawthorne. During the recent President’s Day holiday we ran transportation
service for dialysis customers to ensure they were able to receive their treatments. On March 19
at 10am, the senior center we will be hosting, Metro’s “On the Move Program,” which is a program
that Metro sponsors by training senior volunteers on how to navigate the public transportation
system. One of our very own seniors is volunteering and being trained to participate in the
program in efforts to coordinate taking planned trips with other fellow seniors in hopes that seniors
can enjoy getting out and going sight-seeing. We look forward to continuing to provide the best
possible service for our seniors and disabled community.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Director Thomas
Uwal reported on the following: L.A. 28 Summer Olympics - The L.A. 28 Summer Olympics will be
held Friday, July 14, 2028, to Sunday, July 30, 2028. SoFi Stadium will serve as the host venue for
the opening ceremony. In preparation for the event, L.A. 28 is meeting and collaborating with
various City of Inglewood departments to assess the impact on municipal services and local
residents. Park Maintenance Building Relocation - We plan to relocate our Parks Division staff
from Edward Vincent, Jr. Park to the Inglewood City Service Center. The current office at the park

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

is outdated, and the City is will construct a new facility. The existing building is slated for demolition
next year, and staff will be temporarily housed in the City garage until the new building is
completed. Celebrate Earth Day at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park - The City of Inglewood will host an
Earth Day Celebration on Saturday, April 26, 2025, at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park from 9:00 a.m. to
12:00 noon. The event will include tree planting and park clean-up activities. We cordially invite
our Park, Recreation and Community Services Commissioners to join us for the festivities. At our
last commission meeting, we reported that the Inglewood Jazz Festival was scheduled for Saturday,
June 28, 2025 however, the City has since rescheduled the event to Saturday, July 5, 2025, and it
will be rebranded as the Inglewood Independence Day Music Festival to coincide with
Independence Day.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Padilla thanked all of the divisions and staff members
for their hard work. Commissioner Beck reiterated the gratitude and appreciation for staff
members. Commissioner Beck also acknowledged seeing Director Uwal on television while
watching the Clippers game as he was hosting some of our local seniors. While thanking Director
Uwal for honoring local programs, he also expressed concern regarding Senior and Youth
programs. He suggested that the Commissioners and staff members keep possible funding cuts on
a federal level in mind. He also suggested that fundraising ideas and contingency plans be
considered and planned out in case mass program cuts are set in place. Commissioner Denmon
agreed and thanked Commissioner Beck for the suggestions.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the meeting
adjourned at the hour of 6:47 p.m.
